question: Does response-only training of a repeated native last layer improve both-member correctness on independent human-edited BoolQ questions and shared-prefix yes/no evidence judgments?
gate: Thirty-two unique publisher contrast paragraphs with one original question and one human edit carrying the opposite answer. Require at least five net completely correct pairs, paired two-sided exact p<=.05 at passage level, at least three additional correct common-prefix label judgments, and actual total generation seconds <=Base. If positive train the same one-pass control and test paired transfer. If negative close depth attribution and deployment for this fit. Stop on memory warning or resource budget.
protocol: Train on 1536 distinct passages balanced by answer from the official BoolQ training split; exclude normalized test paragraphs, original questions, and all published perturbations. No edits are used in training. Evaluate both models in thinking mode with identical initial IDs, answer prefix, ordered questions, 384-token output allowance and scorer. Score completion with leading yes/no at a line boundary after closing thinking, and score yes vs no at an identical answer-only prefix. Record both times separately. All fitting and inference on native Metal.
